clue.text: Accomplished line inspiring old man

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the line takes the old man into itself

parts.note: a cable is a line, as in a telegraph or power line
old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: A skilled telephone engineer whose dad was the inspiration behind his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accomplished at a task is competent and skilled, so the adjective works as a synonym.

clue.text: Order digit finally to poke patient

indicators.note: poking is pushing into something, so the letter is pushed inside the patient

parts.note: in medicine a patient under care is a case

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word digit

explanation.surface: A doctor ordering a finger to be used to prod a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A social order or rank in a rigid hierarchy is a synonym for this class division.

clue.text: Issue for one breaking wind — critical moment

parts.note: an issue under discussion is a point

indicators.note: the words for one are broken up and their letters rearranged

parts.note: to wind a road or river is to turn

explanation.surface: A digestive complaint described with medical delicacy, then a dramatic turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges the letters of 'for one' to OFNORE; 'wind' suggests flatulence but is the verb meaning bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage beyond which one cannot go back is a decisive, critical moment in any venture.

clue.text: See 13
Italian author in uplifting procession

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up reads the hidden letters from bottom to top
in tells us the letters sit inside the word procession

explanation.surface: An Italian writer carried shoulder-high in a joyful parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds OCE inside procession and 'uplifting' turns it round to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist and semiotician, author of The Name of the Rose.

clue.text: See 20
Old Independent journalist covering parts say penned by poet

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the poet's name surrounds what comes before

parts.note: John Milton was the poet of Paradise Lost

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so the covering splits the abbreviation

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
skin is a natural covering

explanation.surface: A former newspaper writer whose bits were written up by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' builds ESKING, which 'penned by' places inside the poet; Kington is also the name of a small Herefordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Kington was a humorous columnist who wrote for this newspaper for many years until his death in 2008.

clue.text: Irish writer's novel, most inferior part sent up

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point of anything

explanation.surface: A critic mocking the worst section of an Irish author's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses NADIR to RIDAN; the 's of writer's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, Dublin-born playwright of The Rivals and The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Tory bullshit compounded with age, that cannot be denied

indicators.note: compounded means mixed together, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A jibe that Conservative nonsense only grows worse as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compounded' rearranges the letters of TORY BULLSHIT plus AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely correct is beyond dispute, so the phrase describes a claim no one can deny.

clue.text: Quite so, niche fabricated houses

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
fabricated means made up, so the letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: so as an intensifier means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: Agreeing that an alcove has been built to hold houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' makes EINCH, and 'houses' sets the intensifier after its E; 'Quite' is the definition, not part of the agreeing 'Quite so'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely or in every respect, as quite does in quite right.

clue.text: Sweet, so-called character of Heidi?

indicators.note: so-called signals that the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: Heidi is a Swiss girl, so playing her is a Swiss role

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Heidi, the girl of the Alps, has a sweet nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like a description of Heidi's nature but is the definition; 'character' means a part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake rolled round jam or cream, a British teatime sweet.

clue.text: Result seen as huge, odds cut

indicators.note: cutting the odd letters leaves the even ones, second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A report that an outcome looked enormous once the betting odds were reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, result means follow as a consequence, the same as the answer.

clue.text: Highest and lowest function values are met with ten changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A maths lesson where peaks and troughs of a graph shift when ten is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles ARE MET together with X.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the maxima and minima of a function are collectively its extreme points.

clue.text: Scratching head, sad one has lost British allies — farewell

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the opening letter of sad

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the European Union is the group of allies Britain lost at Brexit

explanation.surface: A melancholy Briton, having lost European friends, saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' drops S from sad, leaving AD; the EU is the partnership Britain left in 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word for goodbye is used in English as a formal parting word.

clue.text: Singer with strapping frame, according to Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their starts

parts.note: strapping means big and burly
a chassis is the frame of a vehicle

explanation.surface: Describing a singer by her sturdy build.
explanation.walkthrough: Chassis is said 'shassy', so swapping the B and SH sounds of burly chassis gives the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Shirley Bassey is the Welsh singer known for the Bond themes Goldfinger and Diamonds Are Forever.

clue.text: Steal fifty two papers

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the i and the FT, short for Financial Times, are two British newspapers

explanation.surface: Pocketing fifty-two sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty two' looks like the number 52; it splits into fifty and two papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is informal for steal, as when a shoplifter pockets goods.

clue.text: Fancy song and dance, very hard

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
a song and dance is a fuss, and to kick up a stink is to make a fuss

explanation.surface: Taking a fancy to a showy musical routine, performed with great effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'work like stink' means to work extremely hard or intensely.

clue.text: Crush third bit of garlic, only crumbs left around it?

indicators.note: around it says the plate phrase wraps round the letter picked out

parts.note: when a dish has been eaten only crumbs remain

indicators.note: third bit of picks the letter in third place in garlic

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: crush the garlic, and soon the plate is nearly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a cooking step with the garlic; it is the definition. 'around it' puts R inside DISH EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush someone's spirits is to dismay and discourage them, as this verb means.

clue.text: Part of number missing leader in god

indicators.note: missing its leader means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a chorus is part of a musical number or song

explanation.surface: A piece of a song without its lead singer, performed in worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing leader' drops the C from CHORUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky deity of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Superlatively clever as an anagram for instance?

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the answer is a rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: Asking whether this is the shrewdest example of a wordplay device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for instance' looks like the usual signal for an example; here instance is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd or astute, so the superlative form means most clever.

clue.text: Range and district reported in flier

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the phrase is said and spelt differently

parts.note: a range is a cooker, a kitchen stove, and a district is a borough

explanation.surface: A news item about a bird seen over a mountain range and its surrounding district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests mountains but is a cooking stove; COOKER BOROUGH said in a British accent gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kookaburra is an Australian kingfisher, a bird, and so a flier.

clue.text: Rubbish bags leaking at home, first of all

indicators.note: first of all picks the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Bin bags splitting at the house, before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is informal for meaningless talk or nonsense, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Get 100% to be sure

definitions.meaning: scoring full marks means getting every question right, with no errors
used for emphasis, meaning certainly or have no doubt

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means commit no error, scoring full marks; idiomatically it means have no doubt.

clue.text: Bone rigid? I'm not so sure

parts.note: stern means strict or rigid
um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Doubting whether a particular bone really is stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Prepared to keep dry wine

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat worn to keep dry
on means ready or set, as in the show is on

explanation.surface: A wine made ready to be kept in a dry cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Prepared to keep dry' is someone with a MAC ON, a raincoat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine from the Mâconnais district of southern Burgundy.

clue.text: Bird: feathers flying in supermarket?

parts.note: Spar is a chain of convenience stores and supermarkets
when the feathers fly there is a row, a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird loose in a shop, feathers everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAR is a European chain of grocery shops common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is a small brown bird, so the answer is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Go north: journey's ending in minute

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate, which is wee in British slang

indicators.note: ending picks the closing letter of the word journey's

explanation.surface: Setting off north, with the trip ending in a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like a unit of time; it is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means very small, which is what this childish word means.

clue.text: Current energy and power source I switched

indicators.note: switched means turned round, so the assembled letters run the other way

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
the sun is the source of solar power

explanation.surface: An electrician switching the current and power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched' turns ESUNI round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something current is presently being used, so the phrase describes what is active now.

clue.text: Joining association, pass comrade

indicators.note: joining means the pass is attached to the association, coming in front of it

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a league is an association of clubs or nations

explanation.surface: Signing up to a club and handing a pass to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joining' places the pass before the association; a col is a dip between mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker, a comrade in the same organisation.

clue.text: Record one's put on the fire

definitions.meaning: a written record such as a ship's journal
a piece of firewood placed on the fire

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a journal of events and a cut length of wood burned as fuel.

clue.text: See 5
Strange throw gully regularly catches

indicators.note: catches means the picked letters hold the next piece inside them
regularly picks every other letter of gully, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: to throw a party is to host it

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: an odd throw caught at gully, a fielding position close to the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: Gully is a cricket fielding position, which makes 'throw' and 'catches' look like cricket terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghostly means eerie or spectral, which is strange in an uncanny way.
